# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in this repository.

## Overview

`neverprepared/homebrew-tap` is a **Homebrew tap** — a data-only repository of
Ruby formula files. There is no application source, no build system, no test
suite and no CI workflow. Consumers install from it with:

```sh
brew tap neverprepared/tap
brew install <formula>
```

Formulae are **generated by each upstream project's release pipeline**
(GoReleaser or a bespoke release workflow) and pushed here. Every file carries a
"Do not edit by hand" banner: hand edits are overwritten by the next upstream
release. Fix a formula in the upstream repo's release config, not here.

## Layout

```
README.md          Tap description + install snippet + tool table
Formula/           All formulae (Homebrew's conventional directory)
  .gitkeep         Vestigial; the directory is no longer empty
  mcp-kroki.rb
  mcp-ms-graph.rb
  mcp-slack.rb
  pbrainctl.rb
  prouterctl.rb
```

## Formulae (live inventory)

| Formula | Upstream | Version | Platforms | Binary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp-kroki` | neverprepared/mcp-kroki | 1.0.2 | macOS arm64 | `mcp-kroki` |
| `mcp-ms-graph` | neverprepared/mcp-ms-graph | 0.2.3 | macOS arm64 | `mcp-ms-graph` |
| `mcp-slack` | neverprepared/mcp-slack | 0.1.2 | macOS arm64 | `mcp-slack` |
| `pbrainctl` | neverprepared/phantom-brain | 3.25.0 | macOS arm64; Linux amd64/arm64 | `pbrainctl` |
| `prouterctl` | neverprepared/prouterctl | 0.2.0 | macOS amd64/arm64; Linux amd64/arm64 | `prouterctl` |

The three `mcp-*` formulae are MCP servers; this tap only ships their binaries
and does **not** describe the MCP tools they expose — that lives upstream. Their
caveats point users at a setup step (`mcp-slack setup`, `mcp-ms-graph setup`) or
at `KROKI_URL` for `mcp-kroki`.

## Two formula shapes

**Public-release formulae** (`mcp-kroki`, `mcp-ms-graph`, `mcp-slack`) are plain
`url` + `sha256` against `github.com/.../releases/download/...`, gated on
`depends_on :macos` plus a top-level `if Hardware::CPU.arm?`. They define
`install` via `define_method(:install)` *inside* that conditional, so the method
only exists on arm64 — a non-arm install fails rather than misbehaving.

**Private-release formulae** (`pbrainctl`, `prouterctl`) come from private
upstream repos, whose plain release-download URLs 404 for token auth. Each
vendors a copy of `GitHubPrivateRepositoryReleaseDownloadStrategy` (removed from
Homebrew core) that resolves the asset id through the REST API and fetches
`api.github.com/repos/.../releases/assets/<id>` with
`Accept: application/octet-stream`. Installing them **requires
`HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN`** to be set; the strategy raises otherwise.

## Conventions

- **Use `on_macos`/`on_linux` + a plain `if Hardware::CPU.arm?` inside**, never
  the nested `on_arm`/`on_intel` DSL blocks. Nested on-arch blocks do not
  register `url`/`sha256` at spec resolution and brew reports "formula requires
  at least a URL". This is documented inline in `Formula/pbrainctl.rb`.
- The vendored download-strategy class is **duplicated verbatim** in
  `pbrainctl.rb` and `prouterctl.rb`. Homebrew loads each formula in its own
  context, so this duplication is intentional — do not try to factor it out.
- Formula class names are the CamelCase of the file name
  (`mcp-ms-graph.rb` -> `McpMsGraph`).
- Version bumps touch `version`, every `url` tag, and every `sha256` together.
- Keep the README's tool table in sync when a formula is added or removed.

## Commands

There is nothing to build. Verification is done with Homebrew itself, on a
machine that has `brew` (this repo's own CI does not exist):

```sh
brew tap neverprepared/tap            # or: brew tap-new / brew tap --force-auto-update
brew audit --strict --online <formula>   # lint a formula
brew style Formula/                      # rubocop-based style check
brew install --build-from-source <formula>
brew test <formula>                      # only pbrainctl and prouterctl define `test do`
```

`brew audit` and `brew style` are the closest thing to lint/test here. The three
`mcp-*` formulae have **no `test do` block**, so `brew test` is a no-op for them.

## Gotchas

- **No CI.** Nothing validates a formula before it lands; a bad generated
  formula reaches users on the next `brew update`.
- Formulae are overwritten by upstream release automation — never treat a manual
  edit here as durable.
- `sha256` values are the only integrity check; a mismatched hash breaks install
  for everyone until the upstream release re-pushes.
- No secrets belong in this repo. Tokens are read from the installing user's
  environment (`HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN`) at install time.
